body:
Subject: TASK-1291 round 1 — finding 1 is live in the store; finding 2 is an undeliverable criterion and needs your ruling

Finding 1 is real and worse than the reviewer could see from the diff alone. The round detector uses contains() on the findings marker instead of the canonical prefix-at-start predicate. I grepped the store: THREE spec files already carry that marker text inside ordinary prose comments — TASK-1-140, TASK-1271, TASK-1205 — including one that merely describes how the findings mechanism works. On any of those specs the detector would advance the round counter and suppress the mandatory round-1 full-sweep prompt, silently defeating the change this very PR makes. Rework queued with those three comments named as the negative-test fixture.

Finding 2 needs YOU, because it is a disposition question rather than an implementation one. The acceptance criterion "measured on the next 20 specs: median rounds-to-merge drops; recorded on this spec as the acceptance evidence" cannot be satisfied before the change ships and twenty specs flow through it. Blocking the merge on it is a deadlock by construction, and the reviewer is correct to mark it unverified — it will be unverified at every round forever. My brief tells the implementer not to attempt it and not to delete it.

Suggested resolution, yours to take or replace: split it into a follow-up measurement TASK blocked-by TASK-1291, and leave TASK-1291's acceptance with only what is verifiable at merge time.

Worth noting because it will recur: this is a distinct failure class from the four in my analysis — an acceptance criterion that is POST-DEPLOYMENT by construction. It is not the implementer under-testing and it is not the reviewer being strict; it is a spec-authoring defect, and I wrote this one. If TASK-1290's criteria gate lands as specified it will flag exactly this shape at done time, on every spec that has one, so it is worth a convention now: a criterion that can only be measured after shipping belongs on a follow-up spec, never on the spec that ships the change.
